title: Playing on the Navy Pier excursion boat and Clark Street
summary: He led a four-piece band of New Orleans men on a Navy Pier excursion boat and played Clark Street, where white Chicago musicians were playing jazz. He does not recall Tom Brown.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Do you remember if there was much jazz on the riverboats at those times, or was it earlier?

You mean here or in Chicago? Well, both here and in Chicago. Well, I used to play on a boat in Chicago at the Navy Pier. That's a recreation pier that extends about a mile, I think, out in Lake Michigan. I used to play on a little excursion boat that makes trips from the pier for a half hour. I used to have a four-piece band there. And I had lucky enough to have three New Orleans men in four in the band. We had four pieces. Like Thomas Taylor, he was on drums. And Alcorn, this Alcorn boy, he was on tenor sax. And Sweet William was on the piano. Myself on trumpet.
Did you notice, did many white Chicago musicians take any notice of the New Orleans musicians, all that style at that time, and try to emulate it?

Oh, yeah, they was playing quite a little bit on Clark Street. I used to play on Clark Street, too. I used to play on Clark Street, too. And I used to come around and sit in, and they could play some nice jazz, too. Was Tom Brown in Chicago at that time?
Well, that was before my time. You mean the saxophone? Tom Brown? No, I'm speaking of Tom Brown, the white trombonist from New Orleans.
Oh. Well, I don't remember. I don't remember. Let's see. It's about the end of the road.
